stops.text: The architecture. A person, a device, an agent, one gate every call goes through, and the tools. Four zones: the managed device, tool traffic through the tool gateway, model traffic through the model gateway, and the control plane of identity, registry, audit and device policy.
Start on the managed device.
The end user. Everything starts with a question they ask an agent.
The AI application, the agent. It is the MCP client. It asks the model for a plan and calls tools through the proxy.
Client policy: which MCP servers the client may load. The allow list, fed from the registry.
OS and app policy. Device policy that closes the side doors: Outlook's automation guard set to deny, and the browser's remote debugging off.
When the agent makes a tools call, it goes to the MCP proxy. How does the request reach the server? Routing, transport bridging, the first hop off the device.
Then the MCP gateway. Should this caller be allowed? Identity, authorization, policy and rate limits, enforced once instead of per server.
The service boundary. Can traffic reach this backend? The network edge in front of the server.
The MCP server. Wrapped where needed, holding an exchanged token, never the user's.
And the tool or enterprise data: the thing the tool call actually touches.
One branch off the gateway: a third-party hosted MCP server. A vendor's server, where its own agent acts under the user's own grant, which your gateway never issued.
Model traffic takes its own road. The agent's prompt goes to the AI gateway. Which model, which provider? Quotas and guardrails on the inference path.
Behind it, the LLM providers.
The control plane feeds all of it.
The MCP registry: what exists, and who owns it. It is the source of the client's allow list and the gateway's routing table.
The model registry: which models are approved, fed to the AI gateway.
The identity provider: OIDC, OAuth, ID-JAG. Single sign-on for the agent, and token validation for the gateway.
Workload identity: which agent is calling, so the gateway knows the workload and not just the user.
GitOps and admission control. No unsanctioned server lands. Servers are deployed from the control plane, not by hand.
Audit and traces. The gateway and the AI gateway send their audit logs here, and the client its traces, every call joined by traceparent.

And the two red dashed lines. Outlook, reached by a script the agent wrote against the mail client's own automation interface. Teams, reached through the approved browser in remote-debugging mode. Both when the gate said no. Neither touches the gateway, and the audit log stays dark along both.
A person, a device, an agent, one gate every call goes through, and the tools. Everything else is that gate done properly.
